title: Bodycam Video Shows NYPD Rushing Man Shot by ICE Agent to the Hospital
excerpt: New footage shows officers racing Oscar Belgal, shot in the neck by an ICE agent with his child in the car, to the hospital themselves — as DHS defends the shooting and Mamdani escalates his fight to push ICE out of New York.
body:
• The NYPD on Friday released body-camera footage from the first officers who reached the scene after an ICE agent shot 28-year-old Oscar Belgal in the neck on Marble Hill Avenue on Thursday; Belgal's 5-year-old child was in the back seat and unhurt.
  • The video shows officers calling for an ambulance, then deciding not to wait — loading the handcuffed Belgal into a police vehicle, rushing him to NewYork-Presbyterian Allen Hospital, and carrying him into the emergency room. His injuries are non-life-threatening.
  • DHS defended the shooting at a Friday news conference, saying Belgal "decided to not comply with lawful orders" and drove his vehicle into ICE vehicles; the FBI and Homeland Security Investigations are now investigating.
  • Mayor Zohran Mamdani said he called President Trump to demand ICE's removal from the city; Trump offered to release Belgal into NYPD custody, and Mamdani declined to detain him — setting up another city-versus-federal standoff.

What the Bodycam Shows

The footage, released Friday by the NYPD, opens with two officers driving up to Marble Hill Avenue, where bystanders can be heard shouting, "ICE just shot somebody!" and pressing the arriving officers: "You got ICE shooting at people?" Oscar Belgal sits handcuffed on the ground next to a gray Honda CR-V, shot in the neck. A man in a reflective construction-style vest carrying a long gun stands nearby — one of the ICE agents, one officer notes: "He's got a gun."

https://x.com/KimKatieUSA/status/2108586808066150434

The NYPD officers, who were on an unrelated call nearby when they heard the shots, radio for an ambulance and then decide not to wait. They lift Belgal into their patrol car and race him to NewYork-Presbyterian Allen Hospital themselves, carrying him from the vehicle into the emergency room. The department stressed its officers responded after the shooting and "had no involvement in the federal operation prior to the shooting," as Commissioner Jessica Tisch put it.

The scene was chaotic: seven shell casings were recovered, the car's windshield bore a bullet hole, and the rear window was shattered. Separate CCTV video obtained by the New York Post shows Belgal hurriedly pulling out of a parking spot on 225th Street as two plainclothes agents approach with guns drawn, one punching and smashing the driver's-side window.

Two Accounts, One Shooting

DHS's version: Belgal, a Dominican national DHS says was in the US illegally and had alleged ties to the Trinitarios gang, was the target of a planned enforcement operation. Agents had tried and failed to detain him in September. On Thursday, according to ICE's Marcos Charles, Belgal refused orders to get out of the car, then "accelerated his vehicle, smashing into two of our government ICE vehicles," weaponizing it and driving toward other officers. One agent fired seven rounds, striking Belgal in the neck.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=o50SBQgToME

Court records show Belgal had a 2023 robbery arrest that ended in a guilty plea to fourth-degree grand larceny with five years' probation, and an August 2025 arrest for selling cocaine and fentanyl in Manhattan — he was out on supervised release. City officials and witnesses tell a different story about Thursday: Public Advocate Jumaane Williams condemned agents who "disguise themselves as construction workers" to shoot a man in front of his child coming home from school at 4 in the afternoon.

"There was nothing that was happening that would make people have to disguise themselves as construction workers, surround a man's car with his 5-year-old son in it, coming from school at 4 o'clock in the afternoon, and shoot him in the neck in the car."

— Jumaane Williams, NYC Public Advocate

Mamdani Versus Washington, Again

The shooting landed Thursday night at City Hall. Mayor Zohran Mamdani, who has repeatedly called ICE an agency that "must be abolished," said he called President Trump directly to demand ICE's removal from New York. In a remarkable exchange relayed by DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin, Trump offered to release Belgal into NYPD custody so the city could pursue its own charges. "I shared that with the mayor. The mayor once again said we will not be detaining him," Mullin said. City Hall has not confirmed Mullin's account.

Belgal has since been moved to a detention facility outside New York state, according to DHS. About 300 demonstrators gathered outside Allen Hospital on Thursday night; police said several protesters were arrested, and another demonstration was scheduled for Friday evening in Lower Manhattan. Rep. Adriano Espaillat, who spoke with Belgal's family, described them as shaken — and said the 5-year-old boy is in good spirits.

What Comes Next

The FBI and Homeland Security Investigations are investigating the shooting, and no findings have been released. For immigrant New Yorkers, the immediate lesson is legal, not political: ICE cannot arrest you at home without a judge-signed warrant, you have the right to remain silent and to ask for a lawyer before answering questions, and city officials continue to insist the NYPD will not participate in federal immigration enforcement. Whether the bodycam video cools tempers or becomes Exhibit A in the next lawsuit will be decided in the courts — and on the streets of Marble Hill.

image_caption: A still from NYPD body-camera footage released October 9, 2026 shows officers attending to a wounded man on Marble Hill Avenue after an ICE agent shot him. Officers are seen carrying the man to a patrol car to rush him to the hospital.
nri_angle: The case tests how far federal immigration enforcement can go in a sanctuary city, and the bodycam footage is now central evidence in that fight — one immigrant New Yorkers of every background, including the city's large South Asian community, will be watching.
author: Diaspora Desk
